title: Gatehouse: Automated Admission, Tensor Conversion, and Profile Publish for OSS LLMs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build an end-to-end intake pipeline (Gatehouse) that accepts community OSS weight submissions, performs deterministic validation, converts tensors into Redwood runtime artifacts, runs lightweight performance profiles, and issues an immutable pin + profile entry into the model catalog. The goal is a reproducible, auditable flow with clear failure modes and automatic rollbacks for bad artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Gatehouse accepts signed manifests and verifies provenance; 2) Conversion produces reproducible runtime artifacts (same checksum across identical inputs); 3) Smoke suite passes on heterogeneous sample inputs within SLOs; 4) Performance profiles (latency, peak memory, token throughput) are published to model-catalog with versioned pin; 5) PRD + runbook published; 6) Automated tests and manual QA approved by infra and security.
decisions:
- Use a two-stage conversion: canonical ONNX intermediate -> Redwood runtime artifact to decouple front-end converters from runtime packing.
- Deterministic hashing to be computed after final packing to create canonical pin.
- Profiling will run on three template sequences (short, medium, long) to capture latency shape rather than exhaustive benchmarking.
- Quantization suggestions will be advisory in the first iteration (no auto-apply).
tradeoffs:
- Slower onboarding throughput vs higher safety (we prefer deterministic conversion and stronger validation over speed).
- Using ONNX intermediate adds an extra conversion step but reduces coupling to many community weight formats.
- Advisory quant recommendations avoids risk of silent quality regressions but means customers may need manual follow-up for cost optimizations.
progress_updates: 2026-02-10: RFC submitted outlining Gatehouse stages and expected artifacts (confluence: https://confluence.redwood/gatehouse-rfc).
2026-02-18: Prototype conversion pipeline validated for small decoder-only Llama-like weights; checksum determinism confirmed across 3 runs.
2026-02-25: Added deterministic manifest validation (signature verification + provenance fields). Found 6 malformed manifests from community samples; raised engagement to submitters.
2026-03-01: Integrated lightweight smoke suite (unit tests + 10-sample model inference) and wired early failure classification (format, shapes, NaN).
2026-03-07: Initial profiling harness wired into CI; however profiling jobs are flapping due to a staging GPU driver bug (tracked in ENG-90312).
2026-03-13: Security review kickoff scheduled; draft runbook posted (https://confluence.redwood/gatehouse-runbook).
blockers:
- Staging GPU driver instability that causes profiling runs to intermittently OOM (ENG-90312).
- Upstream ONNX conversion edge-case causing slight tokenization inconsistency for models with custom tokenizers; awaiting a community fix or we implement tokenizer shim.
risks:
- Incorrect conversion could silently change model semantics; mitigated by reference-output smoke tests and token-level diff checks.
- Publishing a bad profile could mislead customers on performance; mitigated by adding a 'provisional' flag and storing raw profiling runs for audit.
qa_notes: Manual QA performed for 4 community models of different sizes. Targeted token-level equivalence checks and end-to-end inference smoke tests passed for 3/4; the failing model exhibits tokenizer mismatch. Need to add tokenizer mapping layer and re-run.
next_steps: 1) Triage ENG-90312 with infra to stabilise staging drivers; 2) Implement tokenizer shim for custom-vocab models; 3) Add provisional flag and metadata fields for 'profile confidence'; 4) Run full gating across 12 more community samples; 5) Drive security review to completion.
notes_from_reviews:
- PM feedback (Rohit Patel): prioritize clear catalog UX to show 'provisional' vs 'verified' profile states.
- Design feedback (Mariana Silva): catalog UI needs quick link to raw profiling runs and a diff view.
- Infra feedback (Jae Park): recommend throttled profiling queue with backoff to avoid staging saturation.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 1 (internal): Gatehouse enabled for internal engineering submissions, store profiles as 'provisional' (2 weeks).
- Phase 2 (beta): enable for community submissions from whitelisted orgs, show confidence scores (4 weeks).
- Phase 3 (GA): open to all community submissions, automated pin issuance for models passing full gates (6-8 weeks).
monitoring_and_telemetry: Emit events for intake-accepted, conversion-success, conversion-failure, profile-complete, pin-issued. Dashboards: model-onboard-latency, conversion-failure-rate, profile-confidence-distribution (Grafana links: https://grafana.redwood/d/model-onboard).
